ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the circle $\odot O$, $OA=2$, and $\angle ACB=30^\circ$, what is the length of the chord $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOB=2\angle ACB$ and $\angle ACB=30^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOB=60^\circ$,\\
Since $OA=OB$,\\
it follows that $\triangle OAB$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
Therefore, $AB=OA= \boxed{2}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, B, and C lie on the circle centered at O; segments CA and CB form the inscribed angle ∠ACB, and segments OA and OB are radii to endpoints A and B of chord AB. From the text, take OA=2 and ∠ACB=30°. Use the inscribed-angle theorem: the central angle ∠AOB subtending the same chord AB is twice ∠ACB, so ∠AOB=60°. Since OA and OB are both radii, OA=OB=2.
